note: Three non-steroidal FXR agonists (tropifexor, cilofexor, EDP-305) went into second-line PBC on rodent target-gene PD and cholestasis models; all three lowered cholestatic enzymes in 4-12 week phase 2 trials, all three were dose-limited by pruritus that no model carried, and none advanced in PBC. Obeticholic acid is not a member of this tile and is not scored.
label: PBC (FXR agonists)

engagement.note: Tropifexor induced FXR target genes (Fgf15, Shp) in rodent liver and ileum; this PD model, not a disease model, was the engagement read-out.
engagement.short: Tropifexor induced FXR target genes in rodents
engagement.quote: Potent in vivo activity was demonstrated in rodent PD models by measuring the induction of FXR target genes in various tissues.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract names the rodent PD models but not the doses or tissues.
engagement.judgement: Strip opens at the first public rodent PD use for a member drug. Tropifexor's PBC phase 2 (NCT02516605) started 2015-09, before this paper, so the model predates the clinic even though it was published after dosing began.

engagement.note: In the first-in-human study, tropifexor 10-3000 ug raised plasma FGF19 dose-dependently in healthy volunteers: the same FXR-FGF15/19 axis the rodents showed.
engagement.short: FGF19 rose dose-dependently in healthy volunteers
engagement.quote: Single and multiple doses showed dose-dependent increases in fibroblast growth factor 19.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The healthy-volunteer study has no NCT number in the abstract; registry lookup not possible, so registry_date is null.
engagement.magnitude_basis: FGF15 (rodent) vs FGF19 (human) induction, direction only
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Badman 2020 does not put rodent and human data side by side. FGF19 is a direct FXR transcriptional product, so the read-out is proximal rather than downstream. Year is the online date (2019-12-10); print 2020. Two MAD subjects discontinued for asymptomatic transaminase rises, which the PD models did not address.

engagement.note: Gilead's development paper states that cilofexor's rodent intestinal-FXR PD was reproduced in phase 1: FGF19 up, C4 and bile acids down, plateau above 30 mg.
engagement.short: Cilofexor rodent PD reproduced in phase 1
engagement.quote: Cilofexor demonstrated antisteatotic and antifibrotic efficacy in rodent models and antisteatotic efficacy in a monkey model, with the anticipated PD and a manageable safety profile in human phase I studies.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the human PD numbers (FGF19 rise, C4 fall, plateau >30 mg) are from the companion healthy-volunteer paper Younis 2023, doi:10.1111/cts.13469, also abstract-level.
engagement.magnitude_basis: intestinal FXR target-gene induction (rodent) vs plasma FGF19/C4 (human)
engagement.reason: FGF19 rose in humans as FGF15 did in rodents
engagement.judgement: The sponsor states the comparison itself, so comparison_stated is true. The rodent data predate the clinic (cilofexor entered phase 1 around 2015) but were published only in 2024; I have not flagged it as a retrodiction because the model was run before the human answer was known, and say so here. Same status as the 2019 entry, so strengthens: true.

dose.note: The rodent PD models set a target-gene induction target at sub-mg/kg doses; no public rodent-to-human dose projection for any member.
dose.short: Rodent PD target, no public human projection
dose.quote: Potent in vivo activity was demonstrated in rodent PD models by measuring the induction of FXR target genes in various tissues.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract gives no doses, exposures or projected human dose. The full text (paywalled) may.
dose.judgement: Opener for the dose strip on the only track with a public model-side exposure read-out.

dose.note: Microgram doses that engaged FXR in volunteers were enough: GGT fell 26-72% at 30-150 ug/day in UDCA-inadequate PBC; 150 ug cost 3 discontinuations.
dose.short: ug doses engaged FXR and lowered GGT
dose.quote: By Day 28, tropifexor caused 26-72% reduction in GGT from baseline at 30- to 150-μg doses
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The quote is the first clause of a sentence whose p-value/vs-placebo tail is typeset with italics that PubMed strips; the paper reads p <0.001 at 60-150 ug vs placebo. No numeric rodent exposure target is quotable, so the match is on 'target engaged at tolerated dose and the drug worked', not on an exposure number.
dose.reason: ug doses engaged FXR and lowered GGT
dose.judgement: Year is the registry results posting for NCT02516605 (2019-11-13), which carried the per-dose GGT fold changes (0.74/0.41/0.28/0.31 vs 0.86 placebo); Schramm 2022 is the tier-1 record and sets the status. Scored 'reached, drug worked'. No model stated a tolerability margin, so the pruritus ceiling (3 AE discontinuations at 150 ug; EDP-305 18% pruritus discontinuations at 2.5 mg; cilofexor 7% at 100 mg) is scored once, in safety, not here. EDP-305 and cilofexor have no published rodent exposure bridge in the sources I reached.

efficacy.note: EDP-305 30 mg/kg reduced fibrosis in BDL rats; the fibrosis prediction was never tested in PBC, where the phase 2 trials carried no histology.
efficacy.short: EDP-305 cut fibrosis in BDL rats
efficacy.quote: High-dose EDP-305 (30 mg/kg) reduced liver fibrosis in both the BDL and CDAHFD models as measured by collagen proportional area, hydroxyproline analysis, and fibrogenic gene expression
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; quote ends before the parenthetical p-value, whose symbols PubMed strips.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from the Mdr2-/- mouse: a surgical obstructive model with a fibrosis prediction, not a genetic cholangiopathy with a cholestatic-injury prediction. INTREPID listed ELF/APRI/FIB-4 as secondary outcomes but I did not extract them, so the fibrosis prediction stays untested for EDP-305.

efficacy.note: EDP-305 lowered transaminases up to 53%, portal pressure and periportal fibrosis in BALBc.Mdr2-/- mice with established biliary fibrosis, where OCA did not improve fibrosis.
efficacy.short: EDP-305 improved injury and fibrosis in Mdr2-/- mice
efficacy.quote: EDP-305 potently improved pre-established liver injury and hepatic fibrosis in murine biliary and metabolic models of liver disease, supporting the clinical evaluation of EDP-305 in fibrotic liver diseases including cholangiopathies and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis.
efficacy.judgement: Published online 2020-05-06, the same day Enanta released INTREPID topline; the mice were necessarily run earlier and the paper frames itself as support for clinical evaluation, so I treat it as prospective, not a retrodiction. The no-PBC-model problem is real: Mdr2-/- is a sclerosing-cholangitis model standing in for PBC.

efficacy.note: INTREPID: ALP response 45% (1 mg) and 46% (2.5 mg) vs 11% placebo at week 12, p=0.106/0.063 with 9 placebo patients; absolute ALP, ALT, AST, GGT changes significant.
efficacy.short: ALP response 46% vs 11%, primary not met
efficacy.quote: Percentage of Participants With At Least a 20% Reduction in Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) or Normalization of ALP at Week 12 Compared to Baseline
efficacy.confidence_note: The registry record is a results table, not prose: the quote is the verbatim primary-outcome title and the numbers (45.2 / 46.4 / 11.1 %; CMH OR 5.6, p=0.106 and OR 7.0, 95% CI 0.75-65.22, p=0.063) are its values. The press-release sentence in patient_trials carries the same numbers.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ALP responder rate 46% vs 11%; mouse read-out was transaminases, fibrosis and portal pressure

patient_trials.quote: In the intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis, EDP-305 1 mg and 2.5 mg treatment arms resulted in 45% (n=14/31, p=0.106) and 46% (n=13/28, p=0.063) ALP response, respectively, compared to 11% (n=1/9) in the placebo arm.

efficacy.judgement: This is the main call of the tile. The pre-specified ITT primary (ALP responder rate) was not met and Enanta dropped PBC (press release 2020-05-06, Business Wire 20200506005860), which under the dose table reads 'reached, failed, abandoned' = contra. I scored same + partial instead because the data, not the sponsor's words, govern (decision 13): the direction matched (46% vs 11%, OR 7), absolute ALP change was significant vs placebo (p=0.017/0.021) and so were ALT/AST/GGT, and the placebo arm held 9 patients, so the miss is a power miss, not a model miss. A reviewer who holds to the primary-endpoint test should flip this to contra with source_calls_it unresolved; the 2023 retro entry below would then need to leave this track. Year is the registry posting (the brief's dating events do not include press releases); the comparison was first public in May 2020. No peer-reviewed INTREPID paper was found on PubMed.

efficacy.note: Run after the PBC trial read out: tropifexor lowered GGT and bilirubin but not ALP in BDL rats, reproducing the GGT-led response seen in PBC (GGT fold 0.28-0.41 vs 0.86).
efficacy.short: BDL rat reproduced the GGT fall
efficacy.quote: However, it was found that the Tropifexor group had statistically significant decreases in the values of GGT, total bilirubin and direct bilirubin (p < 0.05).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of a small single-centre rat study (Acta Cir Bras); it does not cite the PBC trial, so the pairing is mine.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: serum GGT direction, rat BDL vs PBC day 28

patient_trials.quote: By Day 28, tropifexor caused 26-72% reduction in GGT from baseline at 30- to 150-μg doses

efficacy.reason: BDL rat reproduced the GGT fall
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): tropifexor's PBC results were posted 2019-11-13 and this rat study appeared 2021-10. It reproduced the human direction on GGT, the trial's primary, so retro not same. A piglet BDL study (Xiao 2021, doi:10.1111/liv.14906, framed for biliary atresia) is a second tropifexor retrodiction on the same model type and is not entered separately.

efficacy.note: Run after cilofexor's PBC and PSC trials: 10-90 mg/kg lowered ALP, AST and bile acids and reduced fibrosis in Mdr2-/- mice, reproducing the ALP/GGT fall seen in PBC.
efficacy.quote: Collectively the current data show that cilofexor treatment improves cholestatic liver injury and decreases hepatic fibrosis in the Mdr2-/- mouse model of sclerosing cholangitis.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the genotype in the quote is typeset as a superscript in the paper and PubMed strips it, so the exact characters (Mdr2-/- vs Mdr2−/−) may differ. Patient side: cilofexor's PBC phase 2 (NCT02943447, 71 non-cirrhotic patients, 30/100 mg x 12 weeks) exists only as AASLD 2019 abstract 45 (Hepatology 70 Suppl 1:31A), which I did not open; ALP -13.8% (p=0.005) and GGT -47.7% at 100 mg are from conference coverage. The registry record carries safety primaries only and no efficacy outcome.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: serum ALP direction, mouse vs PBC week 12
efficacy.reason: ALP fell as the mouse said; trial underpowered
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the PBC trial posted results 2020-01-13 and was terminated 'because of the availability of alternate therapies'; this mouse study is framed for PSC and appeared 2023. Same model system as An 2020 (Abcb4-/- cholangiopathy, cholestatic-injury prediction), so it stays on the mdr2-ko-mouse track. Status retro, never same (decision 10). Low confidence because the patient side is a conference abstract read second-hand.

safety.note: The rodent PD and NASH models tropifexor went into PBC on carried no itch, lipid or liver-enzyme safety prediction.
safety.short: Rodent models carried no safety prediction
safety.quote: Potent in vivo activity was demonstrated in rodent PD models by measuring the induction of FXR target genes in various tissues.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; toxicology for tropifexor is not public.
safety.judgement: Opener at the first public model use for a member; the rodent NASH efficacy models (Hernandez 2019, doi:10.1002/hep4.1368) are the same program and equally silent on harm.

safety.note: Pruritus was the most frequent AE (52.5% vs 28.6% placebo), dose-dependent, with 3 discontinuations at 150 ug; no rodent model had shown it, though rodents can show scratching.
safety.short: Dose-limiting pruritus no rodent model showed
safety.quote: Itch of mild to moderate severity was observed in all groups including placebo but was more frequent at the highest tropifexor dose.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Registry AE table (posted 2019-11-13) gives pruritus in 3/11, 6/9, 5/12, 7/8 at 30/60/90/150 ug vs 6/21 placebo.
safety.reason: Dose-limiting pruritus no rodent model showed
safety.judgement: Silence contradicted on a harm the species could have shown: scratching bouts are a standard rodent read-out, and none of the member programs' rodent studies measured them. This is the class's dose-limiting harm in PBC and is counted once, here: EDP-305 2.5 mg had 18% discontinuations for pruritus and 5 severe cases (INTREPID press release; registry pruritus 16/28 vs 3/9 placebo), cilofexor 100 mg 7% discontinuations (AASLD 2019 abstract, read second-hand). The harm was already known from obeticholic acid in 2015, but that drug is outside the tile and its evidence is set aside. Two caveats a reviewer may weigh toward untested: FXR-agonist itch is thought to run through IL-31, which may be human-specific, and tropifexor's registry primary was safety so this trial was built to find it. Lipids moved the other way from OCA (LDL/HDL fell), unpredicted either way.

safety.note: The mouse predicted EDP-305 would not drive the ductular reaction OCA did; INTREPID took no biopsies, so the prediction was never tested, and the mouse was silent on pruritus.
safety.short: Ductular-reaction prediction never tested in PBC
safety.quote: OCA but not EDP-305 at therapeutic doses promoted ductular proliferation in healthy mice and favoured differentiation of primary HPC towards cholangiocyte lineage in vitro.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the quote is the clause after a semicolon.
safety.reason: Stated prediction had no patient histology
safety.judgement: Kept untested rather than contra: the pruritus miss is already scored once on the rodent-fxr-pd track, and the one safety prediction this model stated (no ductular-reaction worsening) had no patient read-out. The INTREPID registry record has the EDP-305 pruritus counts but no quotable sentence, which is the other reason the class miss is quoted from Schramm 2022.

safety.model: PXB chimeric humanized-liver mouse (FXR-agonist induction of human hepatocyte IL-31)
safety.short: Humanized-liver mouse: FXR agonist raised human IL-31
safety.quote: In a humanized liver murine model, obeticholic acid increased IL-31 mRNA expression in human hepatocytes and serum levels of human IL-31.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (open access, PMC9970017). Model side: PXB mice (PhoenixBio, human hepatocytes on uPA/SCID) dosed OCA 10 mg/kg for 18 days; hepatic IL-31 mRNA 7.8-fold, serum human IL-31 1.1 vs 0.085 pg/ml. The abstract quote uses an ASCII hyphen where the typeset text has U+2010.
safety.note: First use of a humanized-liver mouse for the class's harm: an FXR agonist (OCA, not a member) raised human hepatocyte IL-31 mRNA and circulating human IL-31, a pruritogen.
safety.judgement: Opens the only model system found that was built for the class's dose-limiting harm, pruritus. Dated to online publication 2022-07-17 (print Hepatology 2023;77:20-32). The dosed drug is obeticholic acid, excluded from this tile's member list, so product_in_model is false under the sibling-drug allowance; the adjudicator's answer to rule question 7 decides whether this track stands or drops to untested with a note. Safety cell only: IL-31 is the harm's proposed mediator, not the therapeutic PD read-out (FGF19/C4), so no engagement entry is scored from it.

safety.model: PXB chimeric humanized-liver mouse (FXR-agonist induction of human hepatocyte IL-31)
safety.short: Cilofexor raised IL-31 with itch in NASH
safety.quote: In patients with NASH, cilofexor dose-dependently increased IL-31 from Week (W)1 to W24.
safety.magnitude_basis: Mouse: hepatic IL-31 mRNA 7.8-fold and serum human IL-31 1.1 vs 0.085 pg/ml on OCA 10 mg/kg x 18 d. NASH patients (NCT02854605, cilofexor 30/100 mg, 24 wk): dose-dependent serum IL-31 rise; 5.1- to 7-fold higher in grade 2-3 than grade 0-1 pruritus at 100 mg. Different quantities, so direction only.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read. The IL-31 values are not on the registry; registry_date is the NCT02854605 results posting (2019-01-29), which carries the pruritus AE counts (grade 2-3 pruritus 8/56 at 100 mg, 1/56 at 30 mg, 0/28 placebo per the paper's Table 1).
safety.note: Retrodiction in another indication: in the 24-week NASH phase 2, cilofexor raised serum IL-31 dose-dependently and IL-31 was higher in patients with grade 2-3 than grade 0-1 pruritus.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: FXR-agonist pruritus was known in PBC from 2015 (OCA) and for the members from 2018-2020 before the mice were dosed, so retro, never same (decision 10). The paper puts mouse and patient results side by side (comparison_stated true) and its conclusion calls the NASH finding a match. Patient side is NASH, not PBC, so it transfers with imported_from (MONDO:0007027, MASH/NASH); the tile's own disease is scored in the next entry. Model drug is OCA (rule question 7).

safety.model: PXB chimeric humanized-liver mouse (FXR-agonist induction of human hepatocyte IL-31)
safety.short: IL-31 flat in PBC patients on cilofexor
safety.quote: In patients with PBC, treatment with cilofexor did not affect serum IL-31 levels in samples collected at W1, W4, and W12 compared to patients receiving placebo
safety.magnitude_basis: The predicted serum IL-31 rise was absent: PBC patients (NCT02943447, n=71, cilofexor 30/100 mg, 12 wk) showed no change vs placebo at W1, W4, W12 (Figure 4A), and VAS and 5-D itch scores did not move vs placebo (Figure S4). Values are in figures only.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read; the PBC IL-31 and itch-score results are reported as figures (4A, S4) without numbers in the text. Quote is from the Results section; the typeset hyphen in IL-31 is U+2010 in the Europe PMC XML. The PBC trial record (NCT02943447, results 2020-01-13) posts safety primaries only.
safety.note: In the tile's own disease the model's read-out did not move: cilofexor left serum IL-31 and itch scores unchanged vs placebo over 12 weeks in 71 PBC patients; the authors call the NASH/PBC split discrepant.
safety.reason: IL-31 up in mice, flat in PBC patients
safety.judgement: The own-disease comparison governs the PBC context and one member's contra beats the imported NASH match on the same track. The model predicts FXR agonism raises hepatocyte-derived IL-31; in PBC patients dosed with a member drug it did not, and the patient-reported itch did not change either, so the IL-31 route is not shown to carry the class's PBC pruritus (tropifexor, EDP-305 were never measured for IL-31). A failed retrodiction is contra (decision 10); magnitude opposite per the brief's rule for a predicted harm signal that never appeared. Caveats a reviewer may weigh: cilofexor was the member with the mildest PBC itch signal, baseline IL-31 in PBC was 6-9x NASH levels (a ceiling), 12 weeks at 100 mg top dose, and the authors read the split as evidence for multiple pruritogens rather than as a model failure (source_calls_it unresolved). If rule question 7 denies the OCA allowance, this and the prior entry drop and the track stays untested.
